scientific_facts.fact: Native three reactions represent cyanase, carbamate decomposition and carbonic anhydrase recycling; one transport assigns periplasm→cytosol cyanate uptake to CynX/P17583. scientific_facts.fact: One native carbonic anhydrase complex contains CynT/P0ABE9 and Can/P61517. Independent reviewed entries and primary results describe separate carbonic anhydrases, not this mixed assembly.

MetaCyc22.5 defines R524-RXN, RXN0-5222 and RXN0-5224 as a bicarbonate-recycling cycle. Its comment explicitly describes unstable carbamate spontaneously decomposing to CO2 and ammonia and carbonic anhydrase requirement at atmospheric CO2. Source layout selects CO2→bicarbonate for the regeneration reaction.

At0.03%CO2, cynT-deficient E. coli retained active cyanase yet could not degrade cyanate/use it as sole nitrogen source;3%CO2 rescued the phenotype. CynX mutations did not alter examined traits and the physiological function was unresolved in this study.

CynT is an oligomeric zinc carbonic anhydrase; isotope evidence establishes bicarbonate as a cyanase substrate and supports carbamate intermediate formation; Can is a separate active carbonic anhydrase. Induced CynT can substitute for Can under stated growth conditions, supporting alternative enzymes rather than a joint complex.

CynS gives net Rhea11120 cyanate+bicarbonate+3H+→NH4+2CO2. CynT and Can each give Rhea10748 reversible carbonic anhydrase chemistry; each zinc annotation is tied to its own evidence. P17583 currently calls CynX an active cyanate importer without an inline evidence code in that function comment, contrasting with the unresolved role in PMID8444806.

Carbamate decay already occurs in the arginine route as RHEA15650. This shared reaction does not duplicate the cyanate pathway; use it as an authority lead and recheck its exact issuing-source chemistry before addition.
